title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-14
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 3NT. South has only 6 top tricks (2 tricks each in spades, hearts, and diamonds). South wins the spade opening lead and does not have time to play on clubs. By the time the ♣A and ♣K are knocked out, the defense will have been able to establish and run the spades.

South can always take at least 4 tricks in hearts. If South can guess the ♦Q, 9 tricks will be easy. South can play either opponent for the ♦Q. By handling diamonds properly, however, South can maximize his chances when he loses a trick to the ♦Q.

South should lead and pass the ♦J. If West has the ♦Q, 3 diamond tricks will be taken and the contract will be made easily by playing on hearts. When East is able to win the ♦Q and clear spades, South must play hearts for 5 tricks.

Due to South's careful diamond play, North has two entries in diamonds to take two heart finesses. South can lead the ♦K and overtake with North's ♦A. South takes a heart finesse and crosses back to the ♦10. South can take another heart finesse and make the contract if East has no more than 4 hearts to the ♥Q.
